Hannah — reviewed the SOW and did a rough margin & risk analysis. Short summary:

- ARR profile (pilot -> annualized): $240k ARR if pilot converts within 6 months.
- Impact of rev-share: the proposed 20% first 12 months reduces Redwood's take on the first-year tokens by ~8.5% of the expected revenue vs standard 15% marketplace split.
- Cashflow: Net90 from activation introduces ~60–90 days DSO exposure; finance flags this as higher than our standard marketplace terms (we typically do Net30 – marketplaces sometimes accept Net60 with approvals).
- Operational risk: deferred billing complicates marketplace settlement flow (AWS/GCP/Azure have different reconciliation windows).

Recommendation:
1) Exec approval required for Net90 + front-loaded rev-share. This is a material deviation from our marketplace guardrails.
2) If execs prefer a mitigated option, propose: upfront brokerage (one-time onboarding fee paid to Redwood at signing) to offset NPV of Net90 + reduce front-loaded rev-share to 16% for months 1–12. That keeps settlement simpler and reduces finance exposure.
3) Add a 6-month performance clause: if usage ramps slower than forecast, rev-share reverts to standard 12% floor and we pause deferred billing extension.

If leadership can sign off on the exception with the mitigations above, legal should draft an amendment and finance will author a settlement schedule for the marketplace.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Adding marketplace/legal constraints from my side:

- AWS private offers do support deferred invoicing but Marketplace disbursements happen on AWS's cadence — we can record a receivable and reconcile, but AWS will require a contract clause that allows Redwood to invoice CloudSilo directly for the onboarding brokerage fee (non-marketplace revenue) so we can get some cash up front.
- Rev-share tiers that change mid-term are executable, but they must be explicit in the offer metadata and in the S3 billing mapping. That adds engineering reconciliation work; we should limit complexity.

Practical counter I would accept if leadership asks for a simpler alternative:
- One-time onboarding fee of $30k (CloudSilo pays within 7 days of signature).
- Rev-share: 16% months 1–12, 12% thereafter (explicit date-based tiers).
- Deferred marketplace billing limited to Net60 from activation (not Net90). Finance will still need an approval memo for Net60 > Net30.

If leadership insists on Net90 and full 20% front-load, state we need a CFO-level approval and a finance escrow arrangement or guarantee.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the analysis. Executive decision: approve a one-time exception with the following mandatory conditions — we will sign off provided these are included in the private offer and the DocuSign envelope:

1) Payment terms: Net60 from activation (NOT Net90). Finance will not approve Net90 except with a third-party guarantee or escrow; Net60 is an acceptable concession for a strategic pilot.
2) Rev-share: 13% months 1–12 (fixed), 12% months 13+ (standard). This is a compromise between their ask and our economics.
3) One-time onboarding fee: $25,000 payable within 7 days of signature (to offset NPV hit).
4) Monitoring & rollback: 6-month performance review; if usage < 60% of forecast, Redwood can reinstate standard billing cadence and revoke the rev-share concession.
5) Legal to add clear settlement schedule and an explicit clause that allows Redwood to invoice non-marketplace onboarding fees directly.

Please have legal/finance draft the amendment and Karthik, please prepare a short memo for CFO sign-off on Net60. Hannah, coordinate a quick call with Sarah and procure@cloudsilo.com to confirm changes and DocuSign the amendment. We need the signed PO by 11/28 as requested.

—Laura
